title: Interactive work on a branch becomes a work item

story.as_a: Mark, working ad hoc in an interactive session
story.i_want_to: have my session's branch become a work item held by my session the moment I start work on it
story.so_that: fleet_dash shows my ad-hoc work beside the loop's, with one record, without me filing anything

rationale: PRD R2: ad-hoc work in an interactive session is a work item too, created when the session starts work on a branch, so fleet_dash shows it. Today a story comes only from an import, an orchestrator's create_story (role :orchestrator) or intake (Loopctl.Delivery.TriageTrigger, lib/loopctl/delivery/triage_trigger.ex:112-113), and an interactive branch exists nowhere in loopctl. The stage machine already has the shape for work started outside the runner: a stage row opened at implementing (Stages.open_for_change_in_tenant_transaction/4, lib/loopctl/delivery/stages.ex:305), which chg's submitted uses (US-47.8).

acceptance_criteria.description: POST /api/v1/work_items (role: :agent, RequireHumanAnchor) with {repo_url, branch, title?, epic_id?} from a holder credential creates one story in the repo's project (Projects.resolve_project/2 on repo_url) already claimed by the caller: agent_status implementing, assigned_agent_id and assigned_holder_id the caller's, a claim lease from Progress.claim_lease_change/3, lifecycle_entered_at set, title defaulting to the branch; a key with no holder gets 403 holder_credential_required.

The story's epic is epic_id when given (it must belong to the project), else the target_epic_id of the project's active intake source; with neither the call is 422 no_target_epic, whose message says to pass epic_id; the story number comes from the same numbering TriageTrigger uses, moved to Loopctl.WorkBreakdown.Stories.next_number/2.

In the same transaction the item gets a stage row at implementing (Stages.open_started_in_tenant_transaction/4, the renamed open_for_change_in_tenant_transaction/4), its branch recorded as the row's branch effect, and an opened stage event plus a claimed item event, each with reason 'interactive work started on <branch>' and the caller's holder.

Opening a (project, branch) whose item's stage is not done or failed, when the caller holds that item or no holder does, returns 200 with that item and creates no second item; an unheld item is claimed for the caller with a claimed item event, so a session that re-registers after its holder lapsed takes back its own branch's item.

Opening a (project, branch) that another holder's open item already has is refused 409 branch_held with story_id and holder_id; opens of one (tenant, project, branch) are serialized by a transaction-scoped advisory lock, so two concurrent opens yield one item.
When the caller already holds exactly one open item whose stage row has no branch, the open records the branch on that item and returns it (200) instead of creating a second item.
A repo_url that resolves to no project of the caller's tenant (another tenant's included) is 404 project_not_found, and the response never reveals another tenant's project.

The MCP tool work_item_open calls the route; the MCP server, on each holder heartbeat, reads the worktree's branch, and when it is neither the remote's default branch nor detached and the holder holds no item on it, calls work_item_open once for it; a 409 branch_held is logged to stderr and not retried for that branch.

test_cases.name: open creates a held item with its stage row and events (DataCase)
preconditions: project with repo_url git@github.com:mkreyman/chg.git and an intake source whose target_epic_id is epic E; holder H (provided by US-52.13)
expected_results: story in E, implementing, assigned_holder_id h; story_stages at implementing with branch fix/gate-lock; opened and claimed events with the reason and actor_holder_id h

test_cases.name: epic resolution and its refusal (DataCase)
preconditions: project P with no intake source; epic E2 in P; epic X in another project
expected_results: {:error, :no_target_epic}; item in E2 numbered after E2's last story; {:error, :epic_not_found}

test_cases.name: re-open is idempotent, an unbranched held item takes the branch, a lapsed item is taken back (DataCase)
preconditions: holder H; a story S already claimed by H whose stage row has no branch; holder H2
expected_results: first returns S with branch b1 recorded; second returns S; H2 gets S with assigned_holder_id H2 and a claimed event; no new story rows

test_cases.name: two holders race one branch (DataCase, committed, ProductionTopology)
preconditions: holders H1, H2 of one agent; async: false with the race named in the moduledoc
steps: Task.async both opens of the same branch
expected_results: one item; the other {:error, {:branch_held, story_id, winner}}

test_cases.name: route codes (ConnCase)
preconditions: holder credentials H1 and H2; a plain agent key; a repo held by another tenant
steps: as H2 on the same branch
as H1 for the other tenant's repo

test_cases.name: MCP opens the branch's item from the heartbeat once
preconditions: mcp-server with stubbed fetch and a stubbed git runner reporting branch fix/x and default branch master
steps: switch the stub to master and run a heartbeat
stub a 409 on a new branch and run two heartbeats
expected_results: one POST /api/v1/work_items for fix/x; none for master; one POST for the 409 branch; tool declared and dispatched (node --test)

technical_notes: Why a route and not create_story + claim: create_story is :orchestrator (CLAUDE.md, Before Changing Any Role Requirement, rule 2), and the claim is :agent exact; a holder holds only its agent-role credential. The open is the holder recording its own work, atomic with its claim, so this story adds to CLAUDE.md beside the KB carve-out: a holder may open the one ad-hoc item it holds, which carries no acceptance criteria and can reach verified only through report, review and verify like any story.

Projects.resolve_project/2 (lib/loopctl/projects.ex:309, resolve_by_repo_url/2 :822) and release 1's projects.repo_key decide the project; intake source target_epic_id: TriageTrigger.target_epic/1 (triage_trigger.ex:190-191); numbering story_number/2 (:290) moves to Stories.next_number/2 and TriageTrigger calls it (refactor, one numbering). Stories.create_story/3: lib/loopctl/work_breakdown/stories.ex:81.

Stage row: open_for_change_in_tenant_transaction/4 (stages.ex:305-350) is renamed open_started_in_tenant_transaction/4 and its chg caller updated (its moduledoc already describes work started outside the runner); it gains a :branch option written on the inserted row with an effect_recorded event, because Stages.record_effect/5 (stages.ex:1512) opens its own with_tenant transaction and may not run inside the open's (stages.ex:125-129). The claimed item event is Stages.record_item_event/4, provided by US-52.16; assigned_holder_id by US-52.14.

The advisory lock key is a hash of (tenant_id, project_id, branch) taken with pg_advisory_xact_lock inside the open's Repo.with_tenant/2 transaction, ahead of the story write and the stage row, per the lock order in stages.ex:62-84 (it is a new first lock, taken by nothing else).

Context Loopctl.WorkItems (the notes context; created here if this story is built first) holds open_interactive/3; WorkItemController holds the route; both 4xx codes go in operation/2 and the MCP description.

MCP: the heartbeat timer is US-52.13's; the git reads are `git -C <worktree> rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` and `git -C <worktree> symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, run through an injected runner so tests stub them.
non_goals: Moving an interactive item into the loop or back, and keeping an ended session's item out of the loop until Mark moves it: US-52.46 (release 7). Until then a released ad-hoc item is pending like any story, and US-52.46 reserves the ones still unheld at its deploy.
Opening items for runner sessions: their work arrives as placed stories (US-52.15).
Showing the item in fleet_dash: release 5 (README names table: visibility).

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.18.8: an MCP server that cannot reach loopctl simply retries on its next heartbeat; nothing is created locally, and the open is idempotent (AC-52.18.4).
failure_modes.state: AC-52.18.3: the item, its holder, its stage row and its branch are rows in loopctl; the session holds none of them.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.18.4: a retried open by the same holder returns the existing item; AC-52.18.5's advisory lock keeps two racing opens to one item.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.18.5: a slow second open waits on the advisory lock and then reads the first item, answering branch_held or the same item, never a duplicate.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.18.8: the open is triggered by the session's own MCP process on its machine and runs inline in loopctl's request process; the item is reached by its story id.

defaults: Title of an ad-hoc item: the branch name.
Epic: the repo's intake source target epic; otherwise the caller must pass epic_id.
The MCP server opens items automatically on non-default branches; there is no opt-out flag in this release.
definition_of_done: In an interactive session on minis, git switch -c fix/demo in a chg worktree; within one heartbeat interval SELECT s.title, st.branch, h.host FROM stories s JOIN story_stages st ON st.story_id = s.id JOIN holders h ON h.id = s.assigned_holder_id WHERE st.branch = 'fix/demo' returns one row with host minis.
